sources.entry: ShiftIt - Managing window size and position in OSX. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/fikovnik/ShiftIt) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
ShiftIt - Managing windows size and position.

summary.one_liner: ShiftIt is a macOS menu bar app that moves and resizes windows using keyboard shortcuts, and its maintainers say it is not currently being developed.
summary.what_it_does: ShiftIt is an OS X application for quickly manipulating window position and size with keyboard shortcuts. It installs in the menu bar, which can optionally be hidden, and provides a set of window-placement actions. Cocoa and X11 windows are supported, though some applications may not work correctly. An optional FAQ-described setting makes repeated snaps to the same screen side cycle through half, one-third, and two-thirds sizes, toggled via a defaults command. The README says the project is looking for a new maintainer and there will likely be no further development until that transition is done. The README also recommends a Hammerspoon-based alternative (the ShiftIt Spoon, plus a guide to replicate features).
use_cases: snap windows to halves or thirds of the screen
resize and position windows with keyboard shortcuts on macOS
organize windows from the menu bar
replace a window manager utility on older OS X versions
how_to_run: Download the binary build from the GitHub releases page (OSX 10.7+)
Because the binary is unsigned, right-click the app, choose Open, then confirm Open in the dialog the first time
Or build locally: xcodebuild -target ShiftIt -configuration Release
Build without X11 support: xcodebuild -target "ShiftIt NoX11" -configuration Release
Install via Homebrew cask: brew install shiftit --cask
notable: Keyboard-driven window snapping to screen halves, thirds and two-thirds, with optional size cycling on repeated presses
Optional X11 window support, with a separate NoX11 build target
Lives in the menu bar and can be hidden entirely
Release pipeline automated with fabric, including signing and appcast generation
caveats: README states the project is looking for a new maintainer and further development will likely not happen until that is resolved
The distributed binary is not code-signed, so Gatekeeper requires a manual first-launch override
Some applications (e.g. GTK+ OSX apps) may not respond or behave correctly, per the README's known-problems list
Release tooling requires Python 2 and access to project private keys
